title: What is CAGR? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) is the steady yearly rate at which an amount would have to grow, with gains reinvested, to go from its starting value to its ending value over a given number of years. It turns an uneven multi-year return into one comparable annual figure.

title: What is XIRR? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: XIRR (Extended Internal Rate of Return) is the annualised return on an investment where money goes in or comes out on different dates and in different amounts, such as a SIP. It uses the exact date and size of every cash flow, which CAGR cannot do.

title: What is SIP? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: A SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) is a way of investing a fixed amount in a mutual fund scheme at regular intervals, usually every month, through an automatic debit from your bank account. Each instalment buys units at the NAV that applies on that day.

title: What is SWP? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: A Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) lets you take out a fixed amount from a mutual fund scheme at regular intervals, usually monthly, by redeeming units. The units you do not redeem stay invested, so their value keeps rising or falling with the market.

title: What is NAV? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: NAV (Net Asset Value) is the per-unit value of a mutual fund scheme: the market value of everything the scheme owns, minus what it owes, divided by the number of units outstanding. It is calculated and published for every business day.

title: What is Expense Ratio? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: The expense ratio, or Total Expense Ratio (TER), is the annual cost of running a mutual fund scheme, expressed as a percentage of its daily net assets. It is deducted from the scheme every day, so the NAV you see is already after costs.

title: What is Mutual Fund? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: A mutual fund pools money from many investors and invests it in shares, bonds, money market instruments or other assets according to a stated objective, under a professional fund manager. Each investor holds units, and the value of a unit (the NAV) rises or falls with the fund's investments.

title: What is ELSS? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) is a type of equity mutual fund whose investments qualify for a tax deduction within the ₹1.5 lakh yearly limit under the old tax regime. Every investment is locked in for three years.

title: What is EMI? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: An EMI (Equated Monthly Instalment) is the fixed monthly payment you make to repay a loan, such as a home, car or personal loan, over an agreed tenure. Each EMI is part interest and part principal; the interest share is highest at the start and falls over time.

title: What is Home Loan? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: A home loan is a secured loan from a bank or housing finance company to buy, build, extend or repair a residential property, with the property pledged to the lender until the loan is repaid. It is repaid through EMIs over a long tenure, often 15 to 30 years.

title: What is Repo Rate? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: The repo rate is the interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends short-term money to banks against government securities. It is the RBI's main policy rate, and changes in it feed into loan and deposit rates across the economy.

title: What is TDS? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) is income tax that the payer, such as your employer, bank or tenant company, deducts before paying you and deposits with the government in your name. It is an advance payment of your own tax, not an extra tax, and it is adjusted against your final liability when you file your return.

title: What is Fixed Deposit? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: A fixed deposit (FD) is a lump sum placed with a bank, small finance bank, post office or company for a fixed period at an interest rate agreed on the day you invest. The rate does not change during the term even if market rates move.

title: What is Compound Interest? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: Compound interest is interest earned on both the original amount and the interest already added to it, so your money earns 'interest on interest'. Over long periods it makes savings grow much faster than simple interest, and it is also why long loans cost so much.

title: What is Simple Interest? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: Simple interest is interest worked out only on the original principal, for the whole period of a deposit or loan. Interest already earned does not itself earn interest, so the amount grows by the same rupee figure every year.

title: What is PPF? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: PPF (Public Provident Fund) is a government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year term, open to resident individuals through post offices and authorised banks. Deposits can be claimed as a deduction under the old tax regime, and the interest and maturity amount are tax-free, which is why PPF is called an EEE (exempt-exempt-exempt) product.

title: What is EPF? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: EPF (Employees' Provident Fund) is the retirement savings scheme run by the EPFO for salaried employees, to which both employee and employer contribute 12% of basic pay plus DA every month. The balance earns interest declared every year, 8.25% for 2025-26, and is tax-free on withdrawal after five years of continuous service.

title: What is NPS? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: NPS (National Pension System) is a market-linked, defined-contribution retirement scheme regulated by PFRDA, in which your contributions are invested in equity, corporate bonds and government securities. Under PFRDA's December 2025 rules, non-government subscribers can take up to 80% of the corpus as a lump sum at exit and must use at least 20% to buy an annuity.

title: What is Gratuity? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: Gratuity is a lump sum an employer pays an employee for long service, usually after at least five years of continuous service, on retirement, resignation, termination, death or disablement. Since 21 November 2025 it is governed by the Code on Social Security, 2020, which replaced the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972; for non-government employees up to ₹20 lakh is tax-free.

title: What is HRA? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: HRA (House Rent Allowance) is a part of salary paid to help an employee meet the cost of rented accommodation. Under the old tax regime part or all of it can be tax-free, limited to the lowest of three amounts; under the new regime it is fully taxable.

title: What is GST? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: GST (Goods and Services Tax) is India's single indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, collected at each stage with credit for tax already paid. After the GST 2.0 rate changes effective 22 September 2025, most items are taxed at 5% or 18%, with a 40% rate for a small list of luxury and sin goods and nil for exempt items.

title: What is Section 80C? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: Section 80C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 allowed individuals and HUFs to deduct up to ₹1.5 lakh a year for specified investments and payments, such as PPF, EPF, ELSS, life insurance premiums and children's tuition fees. From 1 April 2026 the same deduction is in Section 123 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. It is available only under the old tax regime.

title: What is Section 87A Rebate? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: The Section 87A rebate cuts the income tax of a resident individual to nil, up to a cap, when total income is below a set limit. From 1 April 2026 it is Section 156 of the Income-tax Act, 2025: up to ₹60,000 for income up to ₹12 lakh under the new regime and up to ₹12,500 for income up to ₹5 lakh under the old regime.

title: What is Old vs New Tax Regime? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: India has two income tax structures for individuals. The new regime, the default, has lower slab rates and a larger rebate but allows very few deductions. The old regime has higher rates but allows deductions such as Section 80C (now Section 123), HRA and home loan interest.
h1: What is Old vs New Tax Regime?

title: What is Standard Deduction? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: The standard deduction is a fixed amount subtracted from salary or pension income before tax is worked out, with no bills or proofs needed. It is ₹75,000 under the new tax regime and ₹50,000 under the old regime, or the salary itself if that is lower.

title: What is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) is a government savings scheme for a girl child, opened by a parent or legal guardian before she turns 10. Deposits are made for 15 years, the account matures 21 years after opening, and the interest and maturity amount are tax-free.

title: What is National Savings Certificate? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: NSC (National Savings Certificate) is a 5-year government savings certificate sold at post offices, with interest compounded annually and paid only at maturity along with the principal. The rate is fixed for the full 5 years on the day you buy, and the deposit qualifies for the Section 123 (earlier 80C) deduction under the old tax regime.

title: What is Senior Citizens Savings Scheme? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: SCSS (Senior Citizens Savings Scheme) is a government savings scheme for people aged 60 and above, and for some early retirees, that pays interest every quarter for 5 years. Up to ₹30 lakh can be invested per person, and the account can be extended in blocks of 3 years.
h1: What is Senior Citizens Savings Scheme?

title: What is Sensex? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: The Sensex is the benchmark stock index of BSE (formerly the Bombay Stock Exchange), made up of 30 large, liquid companies across major sectors. Its movement is widely used as a quick measure of how India's large listed companies are doing.

title: What is Nifty 50? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: The Nifty 50 is the National Stock Exchange's benchmark index of 50 large, liquid Indian companies, weighted by free-float market capitalisation. It is the most widely tracked Indian index for index funds, ETFs and derivatives.

title: What is Demat Account? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: A demat (dematerialised) account holds shares, bonds, ETFs and other securities in electronic form, in place of paper certificates. You need one to buy, sell or receive listed shares in India, including shares allotted in an IPO.

title: What is IPO GMP? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: IPO GMP (Grey Market Premium) is the unofficial premium over the issue price at which an IPO's shares are informally traded before they list on a stock exchange. It is an unregulated sentiment indicator, not an official price.

title: What is Gold Purity (24K, 22K, 18K, 916)? Meaning & Definition | gpaisa.in
metaDescription: Gold purity tells you how much pure gold an item contains, expressed in karats (out of 24) or fineness (parts per thousand). 22K gold is 91.6% pure and is hallmarked 22K916; 18K is 75% pure (18K750); 24K, used for coins and bars, is 99.5% or 99.9% pure.
